references.text: The letter to the Hebrews quotes this verse directly and describes Moses as faithful in all God's house, comparing him with Christ.
The letter to the Hebrews again refers to Moses as a servant who was faithful in all God's house, as a testimony to what would be proclaimed later.
Moses is described as a unique prophet whom the LORD knew face to face, confirming his special position as God's servant.
Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him, showing his faithfulness in God's house (the tabernacle).
Moses is referred to as God's servant, a title that confirms his faithful service.
Moses is called God's servant, confirming his special role and faithfulness.
Moses is described as the most humble of all people on earth, emphasizing his character as a faithful servant.
Abraham was also chosen to command his household, an early example of faithfulness in God's house.
